title: Why a Small Circle Can Look Huge: The Ebbinghaus Illusion Explained
hook: A small circle can look much bigger, just by changing its neighbours.

narration.text: A small circle can look much bigger, just by changing its neighbours.
This is the Ebbinghaus illusion, a trick of visual perception.
Your brain uses surrounding context to judge the size of an object.
When a circle is surrounded by smaller circles, it appears larger.
Surround it with larger circles, and it seems much smaller.
This happens automatically, you cannot consciously override it.
It shows how easily our perception can be influenced by context.
Have you noticed similar visual deceptions in everyday life?

description: The Ebbinghaus illusion demonstrates how our perception of an object's size changes depending on its surroundings. Your brain uses context clues, making identical objects appear different sizes. This short video explains the fascinating mechanism behind this common visual trick.
topic: Why your perception of an object's size changes depending on its surroundings, explaining the Ebbinghaus illusion.
